chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, there is an angel of Allah who calls out every day: 'Beget children for death, collect wealth for destruction, and raise construction for ruin.'
ai.seo_question: What does the angel call out every day regarding the transient nature of worldly life?
ai.summary: In this famous hadith from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) employs a rhetorical device of paradox to highlight the inevitability of death, urging believers to build their lives with the awareness that they are constructing for eventual ruin. This perspective, deeply rooted in Shia contemplative tradition, transforms worldly activities from ends in themselves into means of spiritual preparation, encouraging a state of 'active detachment' where one engages with the world without being enslaved by it. The daily call to 'give birth to death' serves as a constant reminder of the transient nature of existence, aligning human effort with the ultimate return to the Divine.
